keyTerms.definition: An E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets Securin for degradation, activating Separase to cleave cohesins and trigger Anaphase.
A mitotic spindle lacking radiating aster microtubules at the poles (characteristic of higher plants).
Microtubules radiating outward from centrosomes toward the cell cortex.
A pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes formed during Zygotene of Prophase I (contains 4 chromatids = Tetrad).
A Leptotene configuration where chromosome telomeres are clustered on the inner nuclear envelope.
The embryonic flat structure formed during plant cytokinesis by Golgi vesicle fusion at the phragmoplast.
The primary chromosomal constriction that holds sister chromatids together and anchors kinetochores.
An animal cell organelle consisting of two perpendicular centrioles surrounded by pericentriolar material.
An X-shaped site of genetic crossing over between non-sister chromatids visible during Diplotene.
A multi-protein ring complex (SCC1, SMC1, SMC3) that holds sister chromatids together from S-phase until Anaphase.
The physical exchange of non-sister chromatid segments between homologous chromosomes during Pachytene.
A regulatory protein subunit that binds and activates Cyclin-Dependent Kinases to drive cell cycle transitions.
A catalytic protein kinase requiring cyclin binding to phosphorylate target substrates.
The division of cytoplasm following nuclear division (Karyokinesis).
A prolonged Diplotene arrest state in female mammalian primary oocytes during embryonic development.
The final substage of Prophase I characterized by complete terminalization of chiasmata and nuclear envelope breakdown.
The fourth substage of Prophase I marked by synaptonemal complex dissolution and chiasmata visualization.
The separation of homologous chromosomes during Anaphase I.
A nuclear division (mitosis or meiosis II) in which daughter cells retain the chromosome count of the parent cell.
A key transcription factor that transactivates S-phase genes upon release from phosphorylated Retinoblastoma protein.
A brief interphase between Meiosis I and Meiosis II lacking an S-phase (no DNA replication).
The division of the cell nucleus during mitosis or meiosis.
A trilaminar proteinaceous disc complex assembled on centromeric DNA that binds spindle microtubules.
The first substage of Prophase I where chromatin condenses into thin visible threads.
A heterodimeric protein complex composed of Cyclin B and CDK1 that drives G2/M transition.
The equatorial plane of the cell where chromosomes align during metaphase.
Failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during anaphase, resulting in aneuploidy.
The third substage of Prophase I where crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of bivalents.
A transcription factor and tumor suppressor ('Guardian of the Genome') that induces p21 expression upon DNA damage.
A cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor induced by p53 that arrests cells at the G1/S checkpoint.
A specialized microtubular and Golgi-vesicle array assembled at the equator during plant cell cytokinesis.
The transitional phase between prophase and metaphase marked by complete nuclear envelope breakdown and kinetochore attachment.
A non-proliferative, metabolically active resting state entered by cells exiting G1.
A multienzyme complex (Rad51, Dmc1) located at recombination nodules that catalyzes crossing over during Pachytene.
A nuclear division (Meiosis I) that reduces chromosome number by half (2n -> n).
The committed decision point in G1 phase beyond which a cell completes division independent of external growth factors.
A tumor suppressor protein that binds and inhibits E2F until hyper-phosphorylated by CDKs.
An inhibitory protein that binds and inactivates Separase until targeted for degradation by APC/C.
A cysteine protease that cleaves the cohesin complex to allow sister chromatid separation at Anaphase.
A metaphase quality-control mechanism that delays Anaphase until all kinetochores are attached to spindle fibers under tension.
The highly specific gene-for-gene pairing of homologous chromosomes during Zygotene.
A tripartite proteinaceous ladder-like structure holding synapsed homologous chromosomes together.
A multinucleate cell mass formed when karyokinesis occurs without subsequent cytokinesis.
A specialized repetitive DNA structure (TTAGGG) capping the ends of eukaryotic linear chromosomes.
The movement of chiasmata toward the distal ends of chromosomes during Diakinesis.
The second substage of Prophase I marked by homologous chromosome synapsis and synaptonemal complex formation.
